content.text: The document contains no audit, inspection, verification, or records-examination right in favor of Kubient. The only access-related obligation is ordinary service-delivery cooperation.

input.quote: Customer agrees to provide all reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services in a timely and effective manner.
input.rationale: The agreement grants Kubient no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right over AP. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records" and "books" return nothing, and a full read of the Fees and Payment (§5), Use of Service (§6) and General Provisions (§14) sections confirms there is no right for Kubient to examine AP's usage, systems or books. The only access-related obligation on AP is the ordinary service-delivery cooperation covenant in §1 ("reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services"), which is directed at enabling performance, not at auditing AP, and it confers no inspection or remote-system-access right. Because revenue reporting and payment flow from Kubient to AP under §5 (sequential liability, Kubient contracts with Advertisers), there is nothing of AP's for Kubient to audit. The outcome is therefore better than the preferred position — no audit exposure at all — and nothing here approaches the walk-away triggers of unlimited/unannounced audits or remote access to Customer systems. No redline is warranted; adding audit limits would only invite a reciprocal audit right against us. We note for completeness that AP likewise has no express right to audit Kubient's revenue-share reporting, which is a separate issue outside this rule's customer-protective scope.
